clue.text: Dandy Joseph with Lisa blending wine

parts.note: a beau is a dandy, a fashionable man
Jo is a short form of Joseph

indicators.note: blending says the letters of Lisa are mixed together into a new order

explanation.surface: A smart man called Joseph mixes drinks with a woman named Lisa.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Dandy' looks like an adjective praising Joseph, but it is a noun; 'blending' is the anagram signal, giving LAIS.
explanation.definitionFit: Beaujolais is a red wine from the region of that name in eastern France.

clue.text: Live with party whip

parts.note: to be is to live or exist
Labour is a British political party

explanation.surface: Someone lives alongside the party whip, the official who keeps MPs in line.
explanation.walkthrough: 'whip' looks like the party official; it is a verb. LABOUR is the British Labour Party.
explanation.definitionFit: To belabour someone is to beat or thrash them, as one would with a whip.

clue.text: Weapon that will not work in a vacuum?

definitions.text: Weapon that will not work in a vacuum?

parts.words: Weapon that will not work in a vacuum?
parts.note: a gun fired by compressed air needs air to work, so it would be useless where there is none

explanation.surface: A puzzle about which arm fails in empty space.
explanation.walkthrough: The joke is literal: with no air there is nothing to propel the pellet.
explanation.definitionFit: This gun uses compressed gas rather than explosive, so in a vacuum it has nothing to fire with.

clue.text: Newly arrived boy

explanation.surface: A lad who has only just turned up.
explanation.walkthrough: Read as two words, JUST IN means newly arrived; as one, it is a name.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase 'just in' describes fresh arrivals, and Justin is a common male first name.

clue.text: The continental one certainly taking plenty of time

parts.note: le is French for 'the', a continental word
I is the Roman numeral for one
surely means certainly

explanation.surface: A European visitor who is sure to dawdle.
explanation.definitionFit: A leisurely pace is unhurried, so it takes plenty of time.

clue.text: Formerly on a future occasion!

definitions.meaning: ... as an adjective means former, as in '... mayor'
... as an adverb means at some point to come

explanation.surface: A paradox: the past and the future in one word, hence the exclamation mark.
explanation.walkthrough: The two senses point in opposite directions in time, which the '!' celebrates.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means both 'former' (a sometime teacher) and 'at an unspecified later moment'.

clue.text: Lot of goddesses? Only one

definitions.meaning: the ... were three goddesses of destiny, so just one of them is a single ...

explanation.surface: A query about how many goddesses there are in a group.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Lot of' looks like 'many'; 'Lot' alone is the first definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Lot means destiny, and the singular of the mythological Fates names one of those goddesses.

clue.text: Aficionado playing it as a musical composition

parts.note: an aficionado is an enthusiast, a fan

indicators.note: playing suggests the words it as a are being played about with into a new order

explanation.surface: An enthusiast performing a piece of music.
explanation.walkthrough: 'playing' fits the musical surface but signals the anagram (TASIA); note the short 'a' belongs to the fodder.
explanation.definitionFit: A fantasia is a free-form piece of music, often improvisatory in style.

clue.text: Dreadful, some say, or very good

definitions.meaning: the word's original sense was causing terror, a usage only some still keep
in modern use the word means excellent

explanation.surface: An argument over whether something was awful or wonderful.
explanation.walkthrough: 'some say' does not signal a homophone here: it marks the older, rarer meaning of terrifying.
explanation.definitionFit: The word first meant frightening, from Latin terrere, and later came to mean excellent.

clue.text: Master's joint title

parts.note: a lord is a master, and the possessive gives lord's
the hip is a joint of the body

explanation.surface: A boss's shared name or designation.
explanation.walkthrough: 'joint title' reads as a shared title; 'joint' is a body part.
explanation.definitionFit: His Lordship is a form of address used for a peer or judge.

clue.text: Fertiliser obtained from worker by river in Yorkshire

parts.note: to man something is to work it, so a man is a worker
the Ure is a river in North Yorkshire

explanation.surface: Muck collected from a labourer beside a northern English river.
explanation.walkthrough: The Ure flows through Wensleydale in Yorkshire, a county in northern England.
explanation.definitionFit: Manure is animal dung spread on land to enrich the soil.

clue.text: Show disapproval of hardwood, we hear, in shop

indicators.note: we hear says the answer is spoken like the words before it

parts.note: boo is a cry of disapproval and teak a hardwood, together boo teak

explanation.surface: Jeering at hardwood furniture while inside a store.
explanation.walkthrough: 'we hear' says BOO TEAK, said aloud, gives the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: A boutique is a small fashionable shop, especially one selling clothes.

clue.text: Sad girl dropping second half in vehicle reversing

indicators.note: in says the shortened girl sits inside the turned-round vehicle
reversing tells us the vehicle is read backwards, like a car going back

parts.note: a cart is a vehicle

indicators.note: dropping second half keeps only the front half of the word girl

explanation.surface: An unhappy young woman losing part of herself as her car backs up.
explanation.walkthrough: 'reversing' turns CART into TRAC; 'dropping second half' leaves GI of GIRL, which goes 'in' TRAC.
explanation.definitionFit: Something tragic is deeply sad, like the events of a tragedy.

clue.text: Quiz old lover before noon

parts.note: an ex is a former partner
a.m. stands for ante meridiem, before noon

explanation.surface: Questioning a former partner in the morning.
explanation.walkthrough: 'before' looks like a charade signal but belongs to 'before noon', AM.
explanation.definitionFit: An exam is a test, a quiz on what one knows.

clue.text: Person named in the post

parts.note: the one whose name is written on a letter is the intended recipient, not someone in a job

explanation.surface: Someone appointed to a position.
explanation.walkthrough: 'the post' suggests a job; it is the mail.
explanation.definitionFit: The addressee is the recipient whose name appears on an envelope or parcel.

clue.text: Put letters in different order again concerning magic formula

definitions.text: Put letters in different order again

parts.note: re means concerning, about
a spell is a magic formula

explanation.surface: Reshuffling letters once more on the subject of an incantation.
explanation.definitionFit: To respell is to write a word again with its letters arranged differently.

clue.text: Putting up with unpleasant diner with gun

indicators.note: unpleasant suggests the words diner and gun are in a nasty mess and need rearranging

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: Tolerating a nasty restaurant guest who carries a firearm.
explanation.walkthrough: 'unpleasant' rearranges the letters of DINER and GUN.
explanation.definitionFit: Enduring something means tolerating or bearing it patiently.

clue.text: Last character absorbed in act of humiliation in town in south-west

indicators.note: absorbed in says one piece is soaked up inside another

parts.note: a penance is a self-abasing act done in atonement
Z is the final letter of the alphabet

explanation.surface: The final letter swallowed up in a gesture of shame somewhere in south-west England.
explanation.walkthrough: Penzance is a port town in Cornwall, England's south-west tip.
explanation.definitionFit: Penzance is a Cornish town, the westernmost major town in England.

clue.text: Even went first and scored equaliser

parts.note: level means even
led means went in front

explanation.surface: A sports report: a side went ahead, then the other drew level.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Even' looks like an adverb; it is the first piece.
explanation.definitionFit: A team that scores an equaliser has levelled the score.

clue.text: Corrupt socialite with empty coach full of gold …

indicators.note: full of says the socialite and the hollowed coach together are filled with another piece

parts.note: a deb, short for debutante, is a young society woman

indicators.note: empty says the inside of coach is cleared out, leaving its outer letters

parts.note: Au is the chemical symbol for gold

explanation.surface: A society girl rides in a coach loaded with treasure.
explanation.walkthrough: 'empty' leaves CH from coach; DEB and CH together are 'full of' AU, giving DEB-AU-CH.
explanation.definitionFit: To debauch someone is to lead them into depravity, to corrupt them.

clue.text: Yearned after length of yarn, made a mistake right away

parts.note: a hank is a coiled length of yarn

indicators.note: away says one letter is sent off from the word before

parts.note: erred means made a mistake

explanation.surface: Someone longed for wool, then slipped up straight away.
explanation.walkthrough: 'away' takes one R out of ERRED, leaving ERED. 'right away' looks like 'immediately'.
explanation.definitionFit: To hanker is to long for something, so hankered means yearned.

clue.text: … yours truly had reportedly seen

indicators.note: reportedly says the answer is what the words before it sound like when spoken

parts.note: yours truly is I, the writer, and I had shortens to I'd

explanation.surface: Continuing the previous clue: I had, it is said, observed.
explanation.walkthrough: The ellipsis joins this to 18 across's surface. I'D said aloud gives the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Eyed means looked at, so something eyed has been seen.

clue.text: Preserve from doctor having bad meal outside

indicators.note: outside says the scrambled letters sit around the other piece
bad suggests meal has gone off and its letters are spoiled into a new order

parts.note: taken as written
MB, Bachelor of Medicine, is a doctor's qualification

explanation.surface: A physician who has eaten something nasty.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bad' signals the anagram (EALM), which goes 'outside' the doctor's letters; 'from' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: To embalm a corpse is to treat it so it is preserved from decay.

clue.text: What's to be voted on could be moving

definitions.meaning: a proposal put to a vote at a meeting

explanation.surface: A proposal for a vote might be stirring.
explanation.walkthrough: 'moving' looks like 'touching'; it means movement.
explanation.definitionFit: A motion is a formal proposal in a debate, and the word also means movement.

clue.text: Gag found in part of barrel

definitions.meaning: a ... stops an animal or person speaking or biting
the open end of a gun barrel

explanation.surface: A joke turned up inside a cask.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Gag' suggests a joke and 'barrel' a cask; both point to the firearm and restraint senses.
explanation.definitionFit: A muzzle is a restraint over the mouth, and also the mouth end of a gun barrel.

clue.text: Side labour to provide group action

parts.note: a side is a team in sport
labour means work

explanation.surface: A team's effort producing collective endeavour.
explanation.definitionFit: Teamwork is cooperative effort by a group acting together.

clue.text: Indication that's remarkably good

definitions.meaning: as an adjective, ... means notable or outstanding, as in a ... success

explanation.surface: A sign that something is exceptional.
explanation.walkthrough: 'remarkably' does not signal an anagram here; it is part of the second definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A signal is a sign, and a signal victory is a striking, outstanding one.

clue.text: See April adjusting latticework

indicators.note: adjusting suggests the words see and April are rearranged into a new shape

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: An invitation to watch a woman named April fixing a trellis.
explanation.walkthrough: 'adjusting' rearranges SEE and APRIL.
explanation.definitionFit: An espalier is a lattice or trellis on which fruit trees are trained flat against a wall.

clue.text: Watchdog lectures somewhat unpleasant peer

indicators.note: somewhat says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A consumer watchdog gives talks that are a bit disagreeable to a nobleman.
explanation.walkthrough: 'unpleasant peer' reads as a nasty lord; 'peer' is the verb to look.
explanation.definitionFit: To ogle is to stare at someone lecherously, an offensive way of looking.

clue.text: Resolute, put off explosive old copper

parts.note: to deter is to put off or discourage
a mine is an explosive device
d was the abbreviation for an old penny, a copper coin in pre-decimal British money

explanation.surface: Firm in purpose, someone defers a bomb and an elderly policeman.
explanation.walkthrough: 'copper' looks like a policeman; it is an old British penny, D.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone determined is firmly resolved, so resolute.
